BEIJING — China and Djibouti have reaffirmed their support for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, opposing international recognition of the breakaway region of Somaliland. The two countries issued a joint statement Thursday following talks in Beijing between Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Djibouti’s Foreign Minister Abdoulkader Houssein Omar. “Both sides firmly support Somalia in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity, oppose any attempt to gain ‘diplomatic recognition’ for Somaliland,” the statement said.

The market places Somaliland ahead of several Middle Eastern countries, including Jordan, Syria, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, although traders remain broadly sceptical that any additional country will formally join the U.S.-brokered normalisation framework before the December 31 deadline.
